title: Do Phones Hurt Test Scores?
subject: Data and graphs
blurb: The school paper says phones are hurting math scores. The graph looks pretty convincing.
intro: This story ran in the school newspaper last week.
body: Phones are hurting student learning. We asked 200 students at Lincoln Middle School how many hours a day they use their phones. Students who said more than 4 hours got an average of 71% on the math final. Students who said less than 1 hour got an average of 88%. That is a 17 point difference. The graph makes the pattern clear. Our school should take phones away during the school day so that test scores go up.

chart.alt: A dot graph showing hours of phone use across the bottom and math scores up the side. The dots slope downward, but some students with high phone use still scored high.

transcript.text: Reporter: We asked students how long they use their phones each day.
Student: Maybe two hours? I never actually counted.
Reporter: We handed out the survey in one class period.
Principal: These numbers show we need a phone ban.

opening_prompt: Read the story, then look at the graph. They may not be saying the same thing. What is one question you would ask before you believe it? Highlight a sentence, or click part of the graph to show me what you mean.
